questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For me it was important that it wasn't too far away so family and friends could come visit. Also that the facilities seemes nice and that the possible courses I would be able to take sounded interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. And the Exchange coordinater is very nice so even if some information was missing then it was easy to just contact her.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any when I arrived because the move in at the acommodation was just by information on email.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There is an option on campus which is newly build and really nice!! I was soooo happy to live there.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in a 4 bedroom appartment so we shared our kirchen and livingroom but that worked very smooth. And it was totally new so everyone wanted to take good care of it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Just that there is multiple different ways of living here e.g. dorm rooms, 2 bedroom appartments or 4 bedroom appartments. So find something that works for you. But not all students gets housing on campus in The Residence. Some may get dorm rooms off campus and some of those are totally fine but some are also very old and not nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was okay to figure out what to do. And as mentioned before the exchange coordinator, Giulia is veeery nice so it is always possible to contact her. But they needed to verify my identity with a copy of my passport that was signed by KU. But KU didn't understand what I needed when I contacted them so they send me around in the system to other people so that was a bit time consuming for something that shouldn't have been a problem. Just make sure to state what you need and ask if you can come by their office to have them make a copy and sign your passport.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange coordinator Giulia was helpfull from KI and their website also helps. And then Exchange coordinators from Ku also.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got exactly the ones I wanted. I followed their biomedicine 5th semester since I also went on exchange on my 5th semester

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just make sure to have all the right deadlines then it should be fine.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels were totally fine. Compared to Molecular Biomedicine on KU they were a bit lower I think but some parts of the courses were based on their previous courses which I didn't have. That made those parts a bit harder. They didn't really expect us to read anything so that was different than in KU (if you are someone who normally reads what is recommended)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not a lot of reading just a bunch of lectures. And then one course was with a lot of assignments apart from the lectures. And in general there is a bit more mandatory classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Molecular Medicine - Oncology
Molecular Medicine - Cardiometabolic and Infectious diseases

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would really recommend the Oncology course. I'm really ineterested in Cancer and therefor it fit me perfectly and I really liked the course structure. 
The Cardiometabolic and Infectious diseases course was a bit all over the place and not structured very well. But is you are into the topic then I think the course would be good to choose anyways. During the course you get to make a research application which can be usefull in the future to have done before.

questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a free gym at both Solna campus (where I was) and Flemmingsberg campus. In the gym it is also possible to sign up for badminton, floorball, basket or other stuff and also just book courts yourself to play e.g. badminton. 
Medicinska Foreningen also held a bunch of parties. But those you have to pay for. I didn't really go to any but they had some cool dinner parties and them parties.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Deffinately the sports activities at the gym.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You should have a lot of Fika (coffee and a kardemomme bulle) and jsut hang out with friends. Do a bunch of shopping and go to the museums and in general just enjoy this beautiful city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No it was a bit difficult since the iomedicine bachelor is international so only few swedish students were there. But it was nice to get to know people from all over the world.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the fact that rugbrød is very expensive here.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Definately all the kardemomme bulle they have here when they have Fika.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for housing a soon a possoble so you have a higher chance of getting into The Residence (on campus).
Maybe let your parents to drive you here since it's so close. Because then you can bring all your favorite things here. 
Take advatage of all the cool study spots on campus!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know people from a lot of different countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be away from family on the bad days

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
